content:
The image shows a corn leaf with a single large, elongated tan/gray-brown lesion that is cigar- or canoe-shaped, tapering at both ends. The lesion is centered on the leaf and appears to span several centimeters. The texture appears dry and papery. There are also a few small orange-red specks visible on the leaf surface, but the dominant feature is the large elongated lesion.

Key observations:
- Large, elongated (cigar/canoe-shaped) tan-gray lesion
- Lesion is on the leaf surface, elongated along the leaf axis
- The shape and color closely match Northern Leaf Blight (NLB) — cigar/canoe-shaped gray to tan lesions 1–6 inches long
- The lesion does not appear rectangular and vein-bounded (which would suggest Gray Leaf Spot)
- No dark spore pustules typical of rust
- A few tiny orange specks are visible but the dominant lesion is clearly elongated tan/gray

The large, cigar-shaped tan-gray lesion is the hallmark of Northern Leaf Blight.
